preview.author: Alex Bowmer

pick.text: Given the complete absence of first-half goals in Mjällby’s last eight European games, 0-0 at half-time seems like a wise selection here.

preview.synopsis: First meeting between a Kazakh and a Swedish club in Europe in recent years. Writer picks 0-0 at half-time (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Winless in 17 European main draw games (D5 L12), two points in the league phase, 1-1 at Atalanta; no new absentees.
strengths.away: No first-half goals in their last eight European games; Bergstrom and Tidstrand went off injured against Malmo.

preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.text: Ajax have shown that they are capable of taking teams apart, and if they are in the mood again here, over 3.5 home goals seems realistic.

preview.synopsis: Ajax won both earlier meetings by two goals (2005/06). Writer picks over 3.5 home goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: One loss in 12 competitive games (W8 D3), beat Atalanta 2-0 and Midtjylland 6-1; Tsygankov, Caio Henrique and Mokio doubtful.
strengths.away: Underdogs on the road.

preview.author: Chris Wilson

pick.text: This game represents a huge step-up in quality for the Romanian side, so backing Brighton to win to nil may not be a bad choice.

preview.synopsis: Brighton have never faced Romanian opposition. Writer picks Brighton to win to nil.

strengths.home: Beaten 2-0 by Hull at the weekend but still Arsenal's closest challengers; heavily fancied in this competition.
strengths.away: Big step up in quality; won both earlier games against English clubs (Leeds, 1970s).

preview.author: Alex Bowmer

pick.text: Given Egnatia’s failure to turn recent bright European starts into victories, Egnatia to score first but Lincoln Red Imps to win seems enticing here.

preview.synopsis: First Albanian v Gibraltarian European meeting. Writer picks Egnatia to score first but Lincoln to win (no outcome covered by a single result).

strengths.home: Two draws then a 2-0 loss to Craiova (reduced to ten men), outside the top 24; Albanese scores in wins.
strengths.away: Gibraltar side; Toledano's goals tend to come in wins.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: A meeting between two strugglers points to under 2.5 goals being a prime option, especially with shot-shy Getafe involved.

preview.synopsis: First Georgian v Spanish major European meeting. Writer picks under 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Top domestically, lost 2-1 at Copenhagen, outside the top 24 in their first major European campaign; no fresh concerns.
strengths.away: Shot-shy; Boselli missed the weekend through injury.

preview.author: Peter Stavrinou

pick.text: It’s hard to look past backing Lugano to win here as the momentum firmly lies with Lugano.

preview.synopsis: Jablonec face a Swiss side for the first time; Lugano have won two and lost three against Czech clubs. Writer backs Lugano to win.

strengths.home: 23rd after a loss and two draws (1-1 with Riga); at risk of dropping out of the places.
strengths.away: Momentum with the visitors; Dos Santos has eight goal contributions in eight matches; Hanus keeper issue.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: If Hearts can build on their solid recent home form to pose Monaco some problems, then backing Hearts/Draw in the double chance market might be worth considering.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Hearts have one win in four against French clubs. Writer suggests Hearts/Draw double chance.

strengths.home: 8-0 win over Dundee, biggest top-flight win since 1957; one Conference League point so far; Kingsley and Magnusson doubts.
strengths.away: Golovin and Mawissa missed Saturday through injury.

preview.author: Sridhar Bhamidi

pick.text: Neither team has shown enough bite recently, so backing a draw could prove to be a handy choice.

preview.synopsis: First UEFA meeting between Lithuanian and Latvian clubs. Writer backs a draw.

strengths.home: Fourth defeat in seven (W2 D1) after a 4-1 loss; more than two weeks off; already champions.
strengths.away: No new absences; short of bite recently.

preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.text: This game looks set to be pivotal for both teams' chances of reaching the knockout stages, so anticipating a slow burner, both teams to score in the second half appears viable.

preview.synopsis: Pivotal game for both; first meeting. Writer picks both teams to score in the second half (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: One point from three league phase games; Lele banned after a red card.
strengths.away: Kjell Watjen banned; long injury list including keeper Bakker and Castillo.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: With these sides conceding only five goals combined in six league phase matches, this clash appears ripe for under 2.5 goals.

preview.synopsis: The sides have conceded five goals combined in six league phase games. Writer picks under 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Excellent Conference League campaign, out of domestic European contention; Jacob Sorensen leads the injury list.
strengths.away: Missing Tingager and Serra at the weekend.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: Given that they have earned some handsome victories recently, backing Beşiktaş to win by 2+ goals seems sensible here.

preview.synopsis: Besiktas won both earlier meetings (2016/17). Writer picks Besiktas to win by 2+ goals.

strengths.home: Eighth in the table despite two without a win (3-2 loss to Celtic), back-to-back Super Lig wins since; Akdag suspended.
strengths.away: Peretz out since late October.

preview.author: Matthew Billon

pick.text: The contrasting form of the sides points directly to a Bournemouth win here, who look a decent price to take the three points.

preview.synopsis: First meeting; Celta are winless in five against English opponents. Writer backs a Bournemouth win.

strengths.home: Four league games without a win (D2 L2); Borja Iglesias doubt.
strengths.away: Rayan has three goals in four UEL games; Juanlu Sanchez injured.

preview.author: Nathan Evans

pick.text: With Din Zagreb performing well defensively and Bayer Leverkusen losing their last UEL outing, the draw market looks an enticing proposition here.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer picks a draw.

strengths.home: Seven points from four, three clean sheets; at full strength; lost last eight against German teams.
strengths.away: Lost their last UEL game; Terrier out.

preview.author: Matt Jones

pick.text: Marseille’ form at home is a concern, so it might be safer to look at both teams to score.

preview.synopsis: Marseille's home form is a concern. Writer picks both teams to score (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Four-game winning streak ended by a 3-2 home loss to Le Mans; lost four of last six at home; Hojbjerg may return.
strengths.away: No obvious injuries; won the only earlier meeting 1-0 (2005/06).

preview.author: Alex Bowmer

pick.text: Given Olympiacos Piraeus’ strong home form, backing Olympiacos Piraeus to win combined with under 3.5 goals is tempting here.

preview.synopsis: Olympiacos won the last meeting 3-1 (2018). Writer picks a home win with under 3.5 goals.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in 11 league phase games (W7 D4), twelve unbeaten under the current manager; Bailey went off injured.
strengths.away: Modric and Pavlovic out.

preview.author: Tom Penn

pick.text: Ararat-Armenia can’t buy a win in the UEL, so backing Salzburg to win and score 2+ goals given their scoring exploits at home seems a smart avenue to go down.

preview.synopsis: Salzburg have clear class edge. Writer picks Salzburg to win and score 2+ goals.

strengths.home: Lost two of three after defeat at Austria Vienna; no new worries; strong at home.
strengths.away: Cannot win in the UEL; Bravim suspended; Armenian sides have lost all five meetings with Austrian teams 16-0.

preview.author: Ben Olawumi

pick.text: Royale Union SG’ form has been remarkable, and if they perform as well as they have been doing in this season’s UEL, Royale Union SG Union to win both halves looks a likely outcome.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer picks Union to win both halves.

strengths.home: Unbeaten in 90 minutes in all competitions (W14 D6), seven straight wins, led by Zeneli's goals; leaders in Belgium.
strengths.away: Lech have not drawn in nine games against Belgian clubs (W4 L5).

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: As Benfica have won all four of their UEL league-phase games by at least two goals, there could be value in backing Benfica -1.5 in the handicap market.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer picks Benfica -1.5 handicap (covers a Benfica win by two or more).

strengths.home: Three defeats then a 1-0 win over Lillestrom, unbeaten in five (W4 D1).
strengths.away: Won all four league phase games by 2+ goals; Prestianni in form; Aursnes doubtful.

preview.synopsis: Doncaster won their last four home meetings with Huddersfield; Huddersfield are far better placed. AI stats preview, no writer's pick.

strengths.home: 21st on 13 points (16-24), 2-2 at Bradford City, one win in five; Clifton and Husband doubts, Wallace and Whatmough out.
strengths.away: Second on 29 points (28-13), lost 0-1 to Leicester, three wins in five and three straight away wins.

preview.author: Matt Jones

pick.text: Despite their away day blues in this competition, Trabzonspor to win looks the sensible selection here.

preview.synopsis: CSKA have lost five of seven against Turkish clubs; Trabzonspor face Bulgarian opposition for the first time. Writer backs Trabzonspor to win.

strengths.home: Lost twice in 15 games, both in this competition; 3-3 at Botev; one point from three matchdays; Pereira out.
strengths.away: Away blues in this competition; Saviolo scores early.

preview.author: Chris Wilson

pick.text: Considering the form Panathinaikos are in on the European circuit, an away win is priced up rather attractively.

preview.synopsis: Nordsjaelland have lost their last four against Greek sides. Writer backs an away win.

strengths.home: Beat league leaders Copenhagen 5-0; best in Europe at home; Salquist missed their last game.
strengths.away: In form on the European circuit; Andino injured in the weekend game.

preview.author: Tom Penn

pick.text: Considering the two sides’ respective recent European home and away records, backing a Borac Banja Luka win or a draw as a double chance seems sensible here.

preview.synopsis: No Bosnian side has beaten an Italian one since independence (D1 L3). Writer suggests Borac win or draw (double chance).

strengths.home: Won 4-0 at Zeljeznicar, scoring four in successive league games; lost two of first three; Cipetic, Esiti, Rogulijc and Savic could miss out.
strengths.away: Carnesecchi out.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: This looks like one of the most difficult games of the matchday to predict, so perhaps a draw will eventuate.

preview.synopsis: Red Star won both 2020/21 meetings. Writer calls it one of the hardest games to predict and picks a draw.

strengths.home: Scored one goal across three matchdays, strong defence, four points; Ngom and Burgess injured.
strengths.away: Red Star expected to miss a key player.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: St Truiden side under new management, so backing Hajduk Split to win holds appeal.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer backs a Hajduk win.

strengths.home: Lost 1-0 to Lincoln, beat Lokomotiva 2-1; four-point lead for qualification; won five of six European home games against Belgian sides.
strengths.away: New management; no major injuries.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: This ought to be one of the most one-sided games in this competition, so backing a FC Copenhagen victory by 2+ goals certainly makes sense.

preview.synopsis: Expected to be one of the most one-sided games. Writer picks a Copenhagen win by 2+ goals.

strengths.home: Unbeaten domestically in Andorra but beaten on each of the three matchdays; Berlanga suspended.
strengths.away: Danish teams have won all six meetings with Andorran opponents; Ramaj injured at the weekend.

preview.author: Tom Penn

pick.text: Both sides have struggled for goals in Europe so backing under 2.5 match goals is the logical approach.

preview.synopsis: Braga have never faced a Finnish side. Writer picks under 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Four clean sheets in November, four unbeaten (W3 D1) after one win from mid-September to October.
strengths.away: Struggled for goals in Europe.

preview.author: Peter Stavrinou

pick.text: There should be plenty of goalmouth action here and so both teams to score and over 2.5 goals seems a highly likely outcome.

preview.synopsis: Freiburg lost 3-0 to Monaco in this phase. Writer picks both teams to score and over 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Five straight wins, three clean sheets; no injury concerns.
strengths.away: Missing van den Belt and Bruns at the weekend.

preview.author: Matthew Billon

pick.text: Real Sociedad’s concerning return against English sides could continue here, and backing Crystal Palace to benefit from a new manager bounce with a home win could prove sensible.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer backs a Palace home win.

strengths.home: Four winless games (D1 L3), new manager Thomas Frank lost 3-2 first time; Wharton suspended.
strengths.away: Poor results against English sides; Barrenetxea awaits surgery.

preview.author: Aaron Murphy

pick.text: Both teams’ recent games have featured plenty of goals, so over 2.5 goals in this encounter looks pretty likely.

preview.synopsis: First meeting between Hungarian and Slovenian clubs. Writer picks over 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Four wins from four, beat Milan 2-0; Zachariassen involved in six goals; Yusuf banned.
strengths.away: Recent games have featured plenty of goals.

preview.author: Nathan Evans

pick.text: Given Sturm Graz’s poor recent form and Hoffenheim’s strong home record of late, backing the home win and both teams to score could prove a solid choice.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer backs a home win and both teams to score.

strengths.home: One win from four (D1 L2), 1-1 at Palace after a 91st-minute equaliser; strong recent home record; De Cat and others out.
strengths.away: Poor recent form; winless in five away against German clubs; Khudyakov out.

preview.author: Peter Stavrinou

pick.text: Juventus should prevail but it’ll prove difficult to keep Omonia quiet, hence a Juventus win with both teams to score makes a lot of sense.

preview.synopsis: Juventus have won all seven against Cypriot clubs. Writer picks a Juventus win and both teams to score.

strengths.home: Fifth in the table, beat AZ 2-1, 2-2 with Fiorentina, 4-0 over Venezia; Alajbegovic and Kalulu issues.
strengths.away: Diony scored in four straight matches, all in the opening 25 minutes.

preview.author: Sridhar Bhamidi

pick.text: With Lyon's strong home form, backing a home win looks a safe selection to include in multiples.

preview.synopsis: First meeting; Lyon are unbeaten in four against Norwegian clubs. Writer backs a Lyon win.

strengths.home: New manager Vicens won 1-0 over Lille; two wins in six, one point from the last two UEL matchdays; strong home form.
strengths.away: Jebara doubtful.

preview.author: Peter Stavrinou

pick.text: These two usually deliver entertainment, making the over 3.5 total goals market rather attractive.

preview.synopsis: NEC's first game against a French club. Writer picks over 3.5 total goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Three unbeaten (W2 D1), seven goals in two wins; Schuurs injured.
strengths.away: Rongier and Frankowski unlikely to feature.

preview.author: Alex Bowmer

pick.text: Given how close these two sides are to each other in the table, backing a draw seems logical here.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer picks a draw.

strengths.home: 16th, beat Hapoel Be'er Sheva 2-0, lost 2-0 to Panathinaikos at the weekend; Kodro and Krizmanic out.
strengths.away: One place above on goal difference; no fresh absentees.

preview.author: Ryan Fisher

pick.text: Sparta Prague’s crisis and AZ Alkmaar’ scoring form of late make AZ at a -1 handicap a tempting route.

preview.synopsis: Sparta are in crisis. Writer picks AZ at a -1 handicap.

strengths.home: One win in nine, sacked manager Priske and director Rosicky this week; 13 points off the title pace; Guddal suspended.
strengths.away: Scoring form; won both Conference League meetings last season including 4-0 here; Schouten, Smit and Patati out.

preview.author: John Pennington

pick.text: Sunderland’s poor conversion rate despite creating several chances in Europe, combined with Jagiellonia’s struggles in the league phase, make backing under 2.5 goals in this one a viable choice.

preview.synopsis: First meeting. Writer picks under 2.5 goals (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Unbeaten in Europe before losing 2-0 to Dinamo Zagreb; back-to-back league clean sheets; Ballard, Brobbey and Xhaka out.
strengths.away: Struggles in the league phase; no fresh injuries.

preview.author: Chris Wilson

pick.text: Picking a winner is tough here, but second-half trends of these sides hint that backing Celtic to score after half-time could be a good approach to take.

preview.synopsis: Portuguese teams unbeaten in last five UEL games against Scottish sides. Writer picks Celtic to score after half-time (no outcome covered).

strengths.home: Two wins from four, beat Ararat-Armenia 3-2, back-to-back domestic defeats; Baradji out.
strengths.away: Baur missed the weekend win over St Mirren; no win away to Portuguese opposition in a long while.
